newsitem.title: UK: TABLE TENNIS-CHINESE WOMEN THRASH HONG KONG.
newsitem.headline: TABLE TENNIS-CHINESE WOMEN THRASH HONG KONG.

text.p: China ruthlessly thrashed Hong Kong, the British Colony they are soon to repossess, 3-0 on Sunday to reach the semifinals of the women's world table tennis championships.

The Chinese women, who have won the team event in 10 of the last 11 championships, now face Germany who edged Sweden 3-2 after losing the first two matches. The German women are assured of their first world championship medal since 1939.
Hong Kong lost 3-0 to China in the Asian championships last December and had little hope of turning the tables.

Even world number 10 Chai Po Wa, an international on mainland China before moving to Hong Kong 10 years ago, was out of her depth against the title-holders, who fielded three of the world's top five ranking players.

Deng Yaping, the world champion and Olympic gold medallist won in straight games against Wong Ching and Chai suffered a similar fate against Li Ju. Song Ah Sim was the only Hong Kong player to provide any serious challenge, taking Yang Ying to three games.

Germany's victory was clinched by European champion Nicole Struse who beat German club teammate Asa Svensson in the decider after a disastrous 21-14, 21-6 defeat against Permilla Petterson which had given Sweden a 2-0 lead.
But Sweden's joy turned to agony as Germany swept through the next three matches with Olga Nemes and Chinese-born Jie Schoepp setting up Struse for the final flourish.

South and North Korea, who formed a joint team to win the world title in 1991, dispute the other semifinal. South Korea, runners-up two years ago, were involved in a titanic two-hour struggle against Japan ending in a 3-2 victory.
North Korea had no problems in dismissing Romania 3-0 to set up a potentially volatile semifinal clash against their neighbours from the other side of the Panmunjon line.
The men's competition reached the last 16, defending champions China, Japan, Germany and Belgium having booked their quarter-final births after heading their respective groups.
Sweden, who have met China in six of the last seven finals, could only place second behind Belgium and now face the champions in the quarters providing they overcome England.
